claims.text: Introducing controlled nanoscale compositional heterogeneity creates magnetic clusters at phase boundaries.
Magnetic clusters at phase boundaries enhance local magnetoelastic coupling.
The nanoscale magnetic clusters act as sites for localized magnetostructural transitions.
Localized magnetostructural transitions reduce the energy barrier for magnetic-domain switching.
Reduced barriers for domain switching enhance magnetic entropy change at applied fields below about 1 T.
Limiting strain accumulation preserves low magnetic hysteresis.
The cluster-mediated mechanism preserves rapid thermal conduction and heat exchange.
Nanoscale compositional heterogeneity can improve the magnetocaloric response while maintaining mechanical stability.
A controlled thermal treatment or alloying step can induce nanoscale compositional inhomogeneity and magnetic clusters without causing large-scale phase separation.
Relative to a uniformly processed alloy, an alloy with induced nanoscale heterogeneity should exhibit a higher magnetic entropy change at low applied fields.
Relative to a uniformly processed alloy, the heterogeneous alloy should exhibit a narrower hysteresis loop.
Relative to a uniformly processed alloy, the heterogeneous alloy should maintain rapid heat-exchange characteristics.

The proposed effect should apply near room temperature in alloys with similar crystal structures and compositions when processing produces nanoscale heterogeneity without macroscopic phase separation.
Large-scale phase separation can compromise mechanical integrity.
